documented_limit_or_requirement: MFM chamber down to 0.77 g/h; high-precision analyzers in closed chambers distinguish ~0.0001 g/h (control) from wells
notes: LA program only. Program flow-through detects 20% of wells vs 95% for Driscoll chambers in the same region: implementation or well mix differs; check before trusting the low limit.

documented_limit_or_requirement: DOI main protocol requires a minimum detection limit of 1 g/h or lower
notes: NM only. Reports values down to 0.001 g/h; recurring 0.01 and 1.69 suggest rounding or default values.

documented_limit_or_requirement: Manufacturer lower bound 0.6 g/h; accurate within about +2% at 1 g/h when all gas is captured. Main limitation is capturing all emitted gas. Under-estimates at 40-200 g/h; Bacharach units can under-report by up to ~100x above ~0.4 scfm (~460 g/h) through sensor-transition failure. DOI requires <=1 g/h. In LA the leak point is first located by OGI.
documented_source: Riddick et al. 2023 (Sensors 23:9246); Howard et al. 2015; DOI 2023 guidelines; Santos et al. 2025; Upton et al. 2025
proposed_prior_detection_threshold_g_h: 0.6-2 if the leak is found; finding step inherits the screening method's limit (OGI-first in LA: 20-150)
notes: Two-stage model: P(leak point found) x P(quantified | found). LSU: Hi-Flow 23% vs chamber 96%. Paired wells: Hi-Flow 0 where chamber measured 40-48 g/h (n=2). Values above ~460 g/h may be biased low if a Bacharach unit was used (Semtech units are a different instrument).

documented_limit_or_requirement: DOI 2023 lists laser absorption spectrometers among high-sensitivity instruments
notes: CO (MGGA) and OK. No non-zero value below 1 g/h, consistent with a reporting floor of 1 g/h.

documented_limit_or_requirement: Non-detects are recorded as < 1 g/h, the defined limit of sensitive binary equipment
notes: CO, FL, MI. Seven detects equal exactly 1.0, consistent with the < 1 g/h rule.

documented_limit_or_requirement: Median (50%) detection limit about 20 g/h at 6 m, rising with distance as a power law. Experienced surveyors reached 90% detection at ~7 scfh (5.6-19.5), about 135 g/h (110-375). DOI: less sensitive than binary detectors.
documented_source: Ravikumar et al. 2018 (ES&T 52:2368); Zimmerle et al. 2020 (ES&T); DOI 2023 guidelines; Agogino et al. 2024
notes: Values of 1.0 likely placeholders, not measurements. Need detection-probability curves from Zimmerle et al. 2020.

documented_limit_or_requirement: DOI 2023: binary detectors must detect 100 ppm or better at the point of emission; non-detects are assumed to be 1 g/h or lower
notes: Sensit (377) and Bascom Turner (200) report no detections at all. A concentration reading is not a rate, so recorded zeros are best treated as screening outcomes, not 0 g/h.

documented_limit_or_requirement: DOI 2023: open-path optical screening must reach 100 ppm-m or better at 1 m
notes: AZ, CA, PA; no detections. Same treatment as handheld detectors.
